drills.q: Price an AI study-helper: state the three anchors you compute before picking a number.
drills.a: COGS floor (token math x usage skew, P90 user), value ceiling (tutoring hours avoided x loaded rate, or grade-outcome value), market anchor ($30/user enterprise precedent; consumer-chat anchors). Then packaging: hybrid seat~P80 + credits given AI usage variance.

drills.q: Why is 'AI-powered' not a positioning statement?
drills.a: It's a feature adjective every competitor also claims - it names no category, buyer, or alternative. Positioning picks the judge: name the market category, target segment, and unique attributes vs named alternatives (Dunford's chain). 'AI-powered X' ages in months as capability commoditizes.

drills.q: List the six killers and mark which two die most often pre-GA.
drills.a: Undefined outcome, no evals, unit economics, trust/compliance, workflow non-integration, ownership ambiguity. Most pre-GA deaths: undefined outcome + missing evals (pilots can't prove success so they stall) and unit economics discovered late.

drills.q: VP wants Copilot-style $30/user pricing. Construct the response.
drills.a: Explain what $30 encodes (M365 installed base + distribution + workflow embedment), then price YOUR economics: COGS floor incl skew + validated value ceiling + WTP bands; propose sequencing if $30 is already in the board deck - launch with grandfathering language, instrument realized value, revisit at renewal with data.

drills.q: Design credits for a coding-assistant with median 400 req/mo, P95 3,000 req/mo, COGS $0.008/req.
drills.a: Median COGS ~$3.20/mo, P95 ~$24/mo. Seat at ~$19-29 covers through ~P80-P90 allowance (e.g., 1,500 req = $12 included); beyond it, credits at 3-5x marginal (~$0.03/req); hard cap on runaway loops. Most users never see limits; P95 funds itself.

drills.q: Support-AI vendor wants per-resolution pricing. When does this work and when does it explode?
drills.a: Works when resolution is verifiable both sides (closed without reopen within window) and QA sampling exists. Explodes with definition drift ('resolved' disputes), lagged reopenings, buyer-side data quality issues, or multi-causal outcomes. Contract needs: resolution definition, measurement window, dispute mechanism.

drills.q: Bundled AI dropped margins 12 points. Undo the bundle?
drills.a: Usually no - unbundling reads as a pay-cut. Keep bundle, add fair-use limits, migrate heavy users to higher tiers with credits, engineer COGS down (cascade/caching). Announce nothing; fix quietly. The ratchet lesson: bundling AI raises COGS forever against flat pricing power - decide before, not after.

drills.q: Run a Van Westendorp for your tutoring AI: what four questions, what sample, what traps?
drills.a: Too-cheap-to-trust / bargain / expensive-but-considerable / too-expensive. 100+ real buyers per segment (300+ to split), concrete offer description first. Traps: anchoring on consumer chat prices, power-user WTP skewing means, stated-WTP being perception bands not purchase promises - validate with cohort price tests.

drills.q: Your product gets called 'just a wrapper.' What four properties end the accusation?
drills.a: (1) Proprietary data loop with measured outcome improvement; (2) workflow embedment taking months to rebuild; (3) eval/compliance depth in a regulated niche; (4) distribution advantage. If none exist, the label is correct - fix strategy before messaging.

drills.q: Pilot shows great demos but legal review has stalled it for a quarter. Which killer(s) and countermeasures?
drills.a: Killer #4 (trust/compliance), usually compounded by #2 (no evals = nothing to show legal) and #6 (no owner driving). Countermeasures: PII redaction/data-flow diagrams in the design doc, golden-set eval reports as compliance artifacts, human-in-loop escalation paths, audit logging, one named owner running a weekly unblock cadence with legal's requirements converted into testable gates.
